recipes.name: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (16.25 ounce) package white cake mix (such as Betty Crocker Super Moist)

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Drain canned pineapple into a 1-cup measure. Add water if needed to measure 1 cup. Set aside juice and 9 pineapple rings for the cake. Set any remaining juice and pineapple rings aside for another use.
Melt butter in a 12-inch cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
While butter is melting, combine cake mix, reserved 1 cup pineapple juice, vegetable oil, and egg whites in a mixing bowl. Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed for 2 minutes.

Remove melted butter from the heat and sprinkle brown sugar evenly over top until all the butter is covered. Arrange 8 pineapple rings around the outer edge of the skillet and place the remaining pineapple ring in the center without overlapping. Place a maraschino cherry into the center of each pineapple ring; pour cake batter on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean, about 40 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool in the skillet for 10 minutes; don't let the cake cool too much or it will stick to the pan.

Run an offset spatula around the edges to gently loosen cake. Place a plate over the skillet, then flip and carefully turn the warm cake out onto a plate. Transfer any fruit or glaze that sticks in the skillet back to the cake.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
raw_recipe.description: This classic pineapple upside-down cake is made in a cast iron skillet to create a delicious caramelized brown sugar, pineapple, and cherry topping.

video.description: The beauty of a pineapple upside-down cake is how its base becomes a delicious caramelized topping once it’s done and flipped. In this easy recipe, that base is made with melted butter, brown sugar, and cherry-studded pineapple rings – all arranged under a layer of soft cake (made with boxed cake mix!) in a cast iron skillet. Unlike most other cakes, this one is nearly done once it’s out of the oven since you can skip the frosting and decorating steps. All you need is a good flip (don’t worry – Nicole shows you how) and a bit of whipped cream to top each slice.

review.reviewBody: Made this in a 9x13 pan and it came out looking so impressive! My family said it not only looked better than the ones in the bakery...it tasted a million times better! I used a yellow cake mix since that's what I had on hand and it was awesome.

I made this 2 times in 3 days. Followed the recipe found out all 10 inch skillets are NOT alike. First hint first batch pineapple rings did not fit. Second batch I rolled them up the edges to make room aesthetics great. First batch used yellow cake mix. Second white. Second batch really fluffed up looked like a souffle. Second batch only 1 cup brown sugar. Second batch added some almond and banana extract for aroma and a hand full of shredded coconut to the cake mix. OMG original was awesome, second little touches explosion to the senses. 5 star to original traditional recipe, and right behind it the little tweeks . BTW first time I ever bought/used a cast iron skillet to cook/bake with ever. Anything I can do, you can do TOOOO.

I made this using my fathers recipe. In a 9X13 glass baking dish I layered molassas, then brown sugar. Added 2 1/2 rows of pineapple and cherries folowed by cake mix (substituting water with pineapple juice from the canned pineapples). Baked as directed on mix. It has always been my families favorite.

Pineapple upside down cakes are one of my favorite to make and eat--and this one turned out pretty good. For me, 1 1/2 cups brown sugar in the topping was too much and made it too sweet (my favorite upside down cake recipe uses only 2/3 cup brown sugar). I also prefer using a butter or yellow cake mix versus a white cake. Those are my personal taste preferences, though. I opted to make this in a 10 inch tube pan, and made a scalloped pattern with the pineapple rings cut in half for a different look. Thanks for the recipe!
I used a 9x13 pan and made brown butter on the bottom and covered it with crushed pineapple and a whole jar of maraschino cherries. It is delicious!

I have made this recipe for over 50 years. Perfect the way written with a 12" cast iron skillet or a 9"X13" baking dish. I have had no problems with variations. Subbing other fruits like peaches or apples works out well with this recipe. Using the Splenda brown sugar blend with no sugar added fruit makes it a little lighter on the calories and tastes good. An important part is getting it out of the pan when warm but not hot.

Amazing! The only thing I did different was added rum to my pineapples and cake mix... I used ½ juice ½ rum for whatever liquid amount the recipe called for.... I sprinkled a little rum over the pineapples before adding the cake batter. PERFECT!!

Note to self: Not having a skillet nor round cake pans, I made this in a spring form pan. Like another suggested, I added cinnamon to the sugar, soaked the pineapples in rum, but it really needed to bake much longer than the cake box suggested. The middle was raw. I'll give this another go but use a larger pan. All that goo on top was a keeper!

Followed the recipe as close as possible. Used a 9.5 x 13.5 glass pan and only had a yellow butter cake mix. Prepared the mix using the instructions on box but substituted 1/4 cup pineapple juice vice 1/4 water in the box call for one cup of water. There was only four rings in the can of pineapple so I used a can of crushed pineapple to fill in the bottom of the pan. The crushed pineapple blended with the brown sugar for a nice coating on the bottom (or finished top). Used cherries in the center of the rings but that was only four, so placed more along the edges of the pan for more color and flavor. Omitted the nuts as we have severe nut allergies in the family.

I didn't have an 11 inch skillet, so I used to 9 inch round cake pans. I did 2/3 cup of butter in each and 1 cup of brown sugar in each. Split a can of pinapple rings between the two as well as one box of cake batter. Came out perfect!!!

I used the cup of pineapple juice in a yellow cake mix & it is delightful! I put all of the rings in my 9 x 13 after melting the butter & adding 1 1/2 packed cups of dark brown sugar! This is an OMG recipe! I did the appropriate cherry in the center of each slice & next cake gets cherry juice mixed with the pineapple juice! YUMMY! Thank YOU!
Great cake - Moist -Delicious ans Easy!!! Definitely will be made again and again.
Absolutely incredible, made it with my best friend and it turned out beautifully

Usually, recipes are more akin to "The Pirate Code" for me. I followed this one to a "t" because I wanted to have it turn out right the first time. It turned out GREAT. Perfect !!! So yummy. Wife, and I, will be keeping this one.
A classic! Beautiful presentation every time.
My husband loves pineapple upside down cake, and he always goes on about how wonderful this recipe is 😁

I used a 12 inch spring form pan, yellow cake made to box directions using pineapple juice +water. Didn’t have maraschino cherries (I don’t buy as we aren’t fans) but it worked out well . I think pecans added to the bottom would be good so next time I’ll try that. Will use about 1/2 brown sugar asked for. Found this overly sweet

I followed his however used yellow cake mix and pineapple juice (no water) and it was good. My cast iron pan is a 12" so maybe I should have used a 10". The cake was delish the next day after being cooled. When we ate a piece the day of baking, after cooled for a few hours, it was a bit crumbly so I am not sure what I did wrong or if this cake is supposed to be more on the crumbly side.
Great flavor! Quite difficult to turn out from cooking pan to serving board or plate!! Mine looked wrecked even planning ahead and being careful! But we all enjoyed the taste!
I love this cake and the cast iron skillet makes it even more inviting!
